nodes.summary: This decision problem accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding, to a k-center instance that is well formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: Generalized nonmetric k-center as a decision problem

nodes.summary: The decision problem of generalized nonmetric k-center on bitstrings is NP-complete: it belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: k-CENTER (GENERALIZED, NONMETRIC) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: Let $(D, K, B)$ be a k-center instance with rows $D_0, \dots, D_{m-1}$, and let $n$ be the length of $D_0$, with $n = 0$ if $m = 0$. For $c < m$ and a natural number $f$, write $D_c(f)$ for the entry of $D_c$ at position $f$, counting from $0$, and set $D_c(f) = 0$ if $D_c$ has at most $f$ entries. nodes.title: Feasible k-center instances

nodes.summary: An instance of generalized nonmetric k-center is a triple $(D, K, B)$ of a finite list $D$ of rows, each a finite list of natural numbers (row $c$ lists the costs from client $c$ to the locations), and natural numbers $K$, the bound on the number of locations, and $B$, the radius.
nodes.title: k-center instances

nodes.summary: A k-center instance $(D, K, B)$ is well formed when all rows of $D$ have the same length.
nodes.title: Well-formed k-center instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
